name: Question 11
problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+t{y}^{′}+2y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+t{y}^{′}+2y=0,\,y(1)=0,\,{y}^{′}(1)=1,\,t>0.
$$
worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(1)=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
0={c}_{1}.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=1,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\sqrt{2}\,{t}^{-1}({c}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)-{c}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute ${y}^{′}(1)=1$ and ${c}_{1}=0$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =\sqrt{2}{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t).
$$

Question 11
?

Given that the differential equation t2y″+ty′+2y=0 has the general solution y(t)=c1cos⁡(2ln⁡t)+c2sin⁡(2ln⁡t), solve the initial value problem t2y″+ty′+2y=0,y(1)=0,y′(1)=1,t>0.

a
 y(t)=12sin⁡(2ln⁡t)
b
 y(t)=12sin⁡(2ln⁡t+2)
c
 y(t)=12sin⁡(2ln⁡(t−2))
d
 y(t)=−12sin⁡(2ln⁡t)
e
 y(t)=12sin⁡(2ln⁡t)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We find the constants c1 and c2 using the initial conditions.

  • Substituting y(1)=0 into the general solution gives 0=c1.

  • To apply the condition y′(1)=1, we first differentiate y to get y′=2t−1(c2cos⁡(2ln⁡t)−c1sin⁡(2ln⁡t)).

Then, we substitute y′(1)=1 and c1=0 into the above gives 1=2c2c2=12.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is y(t)=12sin⁡(2ln⁡t).
